claim: Later.com's June 2026 article recirculates the Billion Dollar Boy 2025 survey figures nearly a year after original publication, indicating the BDB dataset has become a standard industry citation rather than being replaced by newer data.
stance_target: provenance and persistence of the BDB burnout figures in trade press
scope_conditions: Derivative; same n=1,000 US/UK creator sample as the original BDB press release, restated a year later with no new fieldwork. Vendor content (Later sells influencer-program software) with a commercial interest in promoting long-term creator relationships as the solution.
quoted_support: "A 2025 study by Billion Dollar Boy surveyed 1,000 creators across the US and UK and found that 52% have experienced burnout as a direct result of their careers. Nearly two in five said they'd considered leaving the industry entirely."

claim: A 24 Hour Fitness creator program built on a stable, trust-based creator pool (rather than campaign-by-campaign sourcing) achieved 197.8K+ impressions and an 8.4% average engagement rate versus a 2.4% industry benchmark.
stance_target: case study of reduced creator churn improving campaign performance (not a burnout/attrition rate itself)
scope_conditions: Single brand case study cited by vendor (Later) selling the influencer-program software used in the case; no sample size beyond one brand program, no independent verification of the benchmark source.
quoted_support: "The result: 197.8K+ impressions and an 8.4% average engagement rate against a 2.4% industry benchmark."
region: US (24 Hour Fitness is a US gym chain)
